profile.summary: This is a molecular identification test: given one tandem mass spectrum, a model predicts a molecular fingerprint, and that fingerprint is used to rank a pool of candidate molecules drawn from PubChem for the spectrum's molecular formula. The pool and the fingerprints come from the MIST codebase and its public CANOPUS data set, which the MIST authors have since renamed NPLIB1. The record holds the version of this evaluation reported by the DreaMS paper, whose Extended Data Table 1 prints retrieval accuracy at top 1 to top 200 and the cosine similarity between predicted and true fingerprints for feed-forward, MIST and DreaMS models. It is useful to anyone comparing methods that annotate untargeted metabolomics spectra by database lookup.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: The capability under test is structure annotation from a single spectrum without a reference spectrum of the same molecule. A model reads the spectrum, outputs a molecular fingerprint, and the fingerprint is compared with the fingerprints of candidate molecules to rank them. What is scored is whether the true molecule appears near the top of that ranking, which is the question a metabolomics analyst actually faces. The evaluation also reports how close the predicted fingerprint is to the true one, which is a different thing: the DreaMS authors note that their model does better at retrieval while scoring lower on fingerprint cosine similarity than MIST, and that the same pattern was reported for SIRIUS against MIST.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: The spectra are the public CANOPUS data set, extracted from GNPS and prepared for the 2021 CANOPUS methods paper, which the MIST repository calls canopus_train and has since renamed NPLIB1. The DreaMS paper describes it as covering 8,000 spectra from 7,000 unique molecules. The candidate pools are built by the MIST codebase: one pool per spectrum, holding positive candidates, which are PubChem molecules sharing the first 14 characters of the InChI key with the true molecule, including the true molecule, and negative candidates, which are molecules with the same molecular formula. The MIST repository stores these pools in an HDF5 file that is not part of the data download because it is larger than 5 GB, and says it is built with the relevant isomers for the data set. Splits are shipped as tables of split name and category with the values train, validation, test or exclude, and the README recommends three named split files for future comparisons.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: A model must produce a fingerprint for each test spectrum. The MIST retrieval script computes a distance between the predicted fingerprint and each candidate's fingerprint, cosine distance being one of the options, sorts the candidates by that distance and keeps the top k. The analysis script then finds the rank of the true molecule in each list and reports, for k in 1, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200 and 500, the fraction of spectra whose true molecule is within the first k candidates, so higher is better. Where two candidates tie in distance the script takes the worse of the two positions, which the README describes as a change from the earlier optimistic reporting. The DreaMS paper reports accuracy at top k for k up to 200, in per cent, counting a hit for any candidate that shares the first 14 characters of the true molecule's InChI key, together with the cosine similarity between predicted and true fingerprints, and notes that this cosine similarity is the inverted test loss. The DreaMS authors state that for this benchmark they did not use their own Murcko histogram split rule for deciding when to stop fine-tuning, as they did for their other tasks, but kept the split of the benchmark established by the MIST authors.

facts.label: Baselines
facts.value: Five reference methods in DreaMS Extended Data Table 1: a feed-forward network predicting fingerprints, with top 1 accuracy 17.309, a feed-forward contrastive model, MIST predicting fingerprints, top 1 29.368, MIST contrastive, and MIST contrastive plus fingerprint, top 1 30.703. DreaMS fingerprint, the paper's own model, reports top 1 32.731. The contrastive variants train with batches of PubChem molecules of the same molecular formula and a noise contrastive estimation loss.

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: The split files mark molecules as train, validation, test or exclude, and the MIST README states that test set molecules must be kept out of the augmented training spectra. The DreaMS authors criticise structure-disjoint splitting of spectral libraries as leaky for fingerprint prediction, because closely similar structures end up in different folds, and that is why they designed their Murcko histogram splits, which they did not apply to this benchmark. No saved file states a structural similarity cut-off used for the CANOPUS split itself.

facts.label: Allowed inputs
facts.value: The spectrum, and whatever derived features a method chooses. DreaMS predicts fingerprints from the raw spectrum in a single forward pass and notes that this avoids assigning chemical formulas to peaks or building fragmentation trees, while MIST is built on molecular formulas assigned to individual peaks and the repository also feeds in subformula and MAGMa annotations. The retrieval step needs the candidate pool for the spectrum's molecular formula.

facts.label: Adaptation
facts.value: Supervised fine-tuning or training on the benchmark's training split. DreaMS fine-tunes its pre-trained network end to end with a cosine similarity loss on the fingerprints; MIST trains its fingerprint model on the same data, optionally with a contrastive model on top and with augmented spectra from a forward model. There is no zero-shot setting.

notes: This record is one paper's evaluation, not a released suite with a leaderboard, so the page is written from the DreaMS paper's Extended Data Table 1 and Methods and from the MIST repository that supplies the data, the candidate pools and the scoring code. DreaMS names the MIST repository without a commit; the files here are from the head of its default branch main_v2 as read on 27 November 2026, and the README's own change log says the analysis in that branch differs from the published MIST paper, including the switch to worst-case tie handling, so the table's numbers may not have come from this revision. DreaMS table numbers are quoted with the surrounding XML cell markup, since each cell is a separate element and a plain run of numbers does not occur in the file. The test fold size is not printed in any saved file: 8,000 is the size of the whole benchmark as DreaMS states it. The eight protocols in the store are the eight columns of that table, seven top k accuracies and the fingerprint cosine similarity.
